title: What a Five-Year-Old Did to the Gods | Dhruva Part 2 of 2

lines.text: What can a five-year-old do that makes the gods afraid?
lines.caps: What can a *five-year-old | do that makes | the *gods afraid?

lines.text: Sage Narada tested him. Go home, child. This path is too hard.
Dhruva refused. So Narada gave him a mantra for Vishnu, and sent him to a forest by the river Yamuna.
lines.caps: A *mantra for Vishnu. | A forest by the *Yamuna.

lines.text: He ate less each month. First fruit. Then leaves. Then water. Then only air.
By the fifth month, he stood on one foot and stopped breathing. The earth began to lean.
lines.caps: One *foot. | *No breath. | The *earth | began to lean.

lines.text: The gods could not breathe. They ran to Vishnu for help.
lines.caps: The *gods | could not *breathe. | They ran to *Vishnu.

lines.text: Vishnu said: I will go to him myself.
Dhruva was seeing Vishnu in his mind, when the vision vanished. He opened his eyes. And Vishnu stood in front of him.
lines.caps: The vision *vanished. | He opened his *eyes. | Vishnu *stood there.

lines.text: The boy could not speak. So Vishnu touched him with his conch, and the words poured out.
lines.caps: Vishnu touched him | with his *conch. | And the *words came.

lines.text: Vishnu promised him thirty-six thousand years as king, and a star that would never move.
lines.caps: *36,000 years as king. | And a *star | that never moves.

lines.text: But in this telling, Dhruva felt ashamed, like a beggar who asked an emperor for a few broken grains.
lines.caps: He felt like a *beggar | who asked an *emperor | for *broken grains.

lines.text: The boy who wanted a seat found one that no one can ever take. Follow for more stories.
lines.caps: A seat *no one | can *take. | Follow for | *more stories.
